[[Utah Utes men's basketball|Utah]] (2013–2015) | draft_year = | draft_round = | draft_pick = | draft_team = | career_start = | years1 = | team1 = | highlights = * Consensus second-team [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] ([[2015 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|2015]]) * [[Bob Cousy Award]] (2015) * 2× First-team [[List of All-Pacific-12 Conference men's basketball teams|All-Pac-12]] ([[2013–14 Pacific-12 Conference men's basketball season|2014]]–[[2014–15 Pacific-12 Conference men's basketball season|2015]]) * 2× [[Pacific-12 Conference|Pac-12]] All-Defensive team (2014–2015) * {{nowrap|2× [[Coast Conference]] Player of the Year (2012–2013)}} }} '''Delon Elijah Wright''' (born April 26, 1992) is an American basketball player who recently completed his college career at the [[University of Utah]] and who has declared himself eligible for the [[2015 NBA draft]]. He is also one of the guards that made all first-team in [[List of All-Pacific-12 Conference men's basketball teams]] in 2014 and 2015. He is the two-time All Defensive team in [[Pacific-12 Conference]] All-Defensive team in 2014 and in 2015. He also earned himself the [[Bob Cousy Award]] in 2015. ==High school and junior college== Born in [[Los Angeles, California]],{{cite web | last = | first = | title = Wright CBSSports.com profile | work = [[CBSSports.com]] | date = | url = http://www.cbssports.com/collegebasketball/players/playerpage/2105158/delon-wright | accessdate = December 22, 2014}} Wright led [[Leuzinger High School]] to the California state championship as a senior and was named [[CIF Southern Section]] Division 1A Player of the Year. Despite his high school success, academics led him to enroll at [[California Community College Athletic Association]] (CCCAA) school the [[City College of San Francisco]]. After two successful seasons there, he committed to Utah over [[Washington Huskies men's basketball|Washington]], [[Washington State Cougars men's basketball|Washington State]], [[Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball|Gonzaga]] and [[Saint Mary's Gaels men's basketball|Saint Mary’s]], despite the Utes winning only 6 games the previous season.{{cite web | last = Johnson| first = Raphielle| title = 6-5 City College of San Francisco point guard Delon Wright commits to Utah | work = [[NBCSports.com]] | date = September 21, 2012| url = http://collegebasketballtalk.nbcsports.com/2012/09/21/6-5-city-college-of-san-francisco-point-guard-delon-wright-commits-to-utah/ | accessdate = December 22, 2014}} ==College career== In his first season at Utah, Wright immediately became one of the top players in the [[Pacific-12 Conference]].{{cite web | last = Hill| first = Bonta| title = Fomer CCSF standout Delon Wright makes seamless transition to Division I at Utah | work = [[San Francisco Examiner]] | date = March 4, 2014| url = http://www.sfexaminer.com/sanfrancisco/fomer-ccsf-standout-delon-wright-makes-seamless-transition-to-division-i-at-utah/Content?oid=2720323 | accessdate = December 22, 2014}} He finished in the top 10 in the conference in [[Points per game|scoring]] (seventh at 16.9 points per game), [[Assist (basketball)|assists]] (third at 4.89), [[Steal (basketball)|steals]] (first at 2.56), [[blocked shot]]s (sixth at 1.3), [[field goal percentage]] (third at 56.1 percent) and [[free throw percentage]] (ninth at 80.5 percent). Wright additionally averaged 6.8 [[rebounds per game]], despite playing the [[Guard (basketball)|guard]] position.{{cite web | last = | first = | title = Delon Wright Utah Utes bio | work = [[Utah Utes]] | date = | url = http://www.utahutes.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/delon_wright_845505.html | accessdate = December 22, 2014}} At the conclusion of the [[2013–14 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2013–14 season]], Wright became the first Ute to be named first-team [[List of All-Pacific-12 Conference men's basketball teams|All-Pac-12]] and was also named to the league's All-Defensive team.{{cite web | last = Facer| first = Dick| title = Utah basketball: Delon Wright makes Pac-12 history for Runnin' Utes | work = [[Deseret News]] | date = March 10, 2014 | url = http://www.deseretnews.com/article/865598328/Utes-Delon-Wright-named-to-All-Pac-12-first-team.html?pg=all | accessdate = December 22, 2014}} Following the season, Wright considered entering the [[2014 NBA draft]], but ultimately decided to return to Utah for his senior season. At the start of his senior season, Wright was named to the 50-man watch lists for the [[Naismith College Player of the Year]]{{cite web | last = Judd| first = Brandon| title = BYU's Haws, Utah's Wright named to Naismith Trophy watch list | work = [[Deseret News]] | date = December 3, 2014 | url = http://www.deseretnews.com/article/865616896/BYUs-Haws-Utahs-Wright-named-to-Naismith-Trophy-watch-list.html | accessdate = December 22, 2014}} and the [[John R. Wooden Award]].{{cite web | last = | first = | title = Utah's Delon Wright Named to Wooden Award Watch List | work = [[Utah Utes]] | date = November 17, 2014 | url = http://www.utahutes.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/111714aaa.html | accessdate = December 22, 2014}} For the second-straight season, he was voted first-team All-Pac-12 and again named to the Pac-12 All-Defensive Team.{{cite press release|title=2014-15 Pac-12 Conference Men's Basketball Honors|date=March 9, 2015|publisher=Pac-12|url=http://pac-12.com/article/2015/03/09/2014-15-pac-12-conference-mens-basketball-honors|archiveurl=http://www.webcitation.org/6WuCA8C5K|archivedate=March 9, 2015|deadurl=no}} Wright was also a two-time member of the Pac-12 All-Defensive team and won the 2015 [[Bob Cousy Award]]. Wright became the first player in Utah men's basketball history to be named to the first-team [[List of All-Pacific-12 Conference men's basketball teams|All-Pac-12]] in consecutive years ([[2013–14 Pacific-12 Conference men's basketball season|2014]] and [[2014–15 Pacific-12 Conference men's basketball season|2015]]). ===College statistics=== {{NBA player statistics start}} |-
